label: Action Footer
title: Action Footer
summary: Keep the next step close to the decision.

anatomy.title: Three parts keep the next step anchored
anatomy.description: The optional title, action group, and token-owned surface form one bottom action region.
blocks: Optional context above the actions. Omit it when the decision is already clear.
A public ButtonGroup or Stack owns horizontal or vertical button layout.
ActionFooter owns background, shadow, padding, radius, and mode resolution.

configuration.title: Choose the title and the action grouping
configuration.description: Use a ButtonGroup for a row. Use Stack when the actions need a vertical reading order.
blocks: Keep the surface short when the preceding content already names the decision.
Add a short title and stack actions when horizontal space or hierarchy calls for it.

states.title: The footer reflects its supplied composition
states.description: ActionFooter does not invent disabled, loading, or confirmation states. Configure those on its public child actions and show feedback elsewhere.
blocks: A lone Continue action receives the full available width.
Back supports the clearly prioritized Continue action.
The owner receives Dark and cascades it through the composite.

sizing.title: Fill the host width and hug the content height
sizing.description: The Figma reference is 360px wide and 93px high without a title. The host supplies width; title and grouping change the natural height.
blocks: Horizontal actions fill the surface while the footer hugs its content.
The composite changes its own height; ActionFooter remains full width.

content.title: Make one action unmistakably primary
content.description: Use short verb-led labels. Keep confirmation or error feedback in the surrounding flow rather than inside the persistent footer.
blocks: Use one clear primary action such as Continue or Confirm payment.
Continue and Back scan faster than sentences that repeat the screen title.
Show confirmation, validation, or failure near the content that changed.

inContext.title: Confirm a reviewed payment
inContext.description: The public footer follows a short Coin composition and keeps the final decision at the bottom of the host.

doDont.title: Protect the action hierarchy
doDont.description: A strong footer makes the preferred next step visible before someone reads every label.
blocks: Back stays secondary while Continue carries the next step.
Equal emphasis hides which action advances the decision.
Back and Confirm payment describe both outcomes directly.
Yes and Go make people infer what will happen next.
A short title adds context without repeating the action.
A long title slows scanning and duplicates the primary action.
specimen: Continue to continue with the next step of your payment

sources.title: Public component, verified behavior
sources.description: The designer guide keeps the Figma reference and package runtime distinct where their bottom spacing differs.
blocks: Public node 2904:8057 · title property, 360px HUG reference
Default, title, 24px padding, and stacked-content stories

The public export is jfs-components 0.1.60. Figma’s sample includes 41px bottom spacing; the package defaults to 24px plus an optional safe-area inset. Web renders in normal flow, native pins the footer, and keyboard avoidance remains consumer-owned.
